slides.title: ViTaR: Visuo-Tactile Residual Adaptation for Foundation VLA Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE RESIDUAL ADAPTATION FOR VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: ViTaR introduces a method to modulate frozen VLA models using tactile feedback for contact-rich manipulation, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: ViTaR improves frozen VLA models by using tactile feedback as a bounded execution modulator for residuals.
card.key_idea: It employs Effect-Guided Modeling to rank residual corrections via pairwise preferences and Residual Action Modulation to select and scale these corrections based on real-time visuo-tactile observations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC benchmark (61.3% success) and physical robots (48.3% success), outperforming frozen OpenVLA-OFT and tactile-fusion baselines.
card.limitation: Absolute performance is constrained by the frozen base policy's semantic action quality.

slides.title: Vision-Based Tactile Intelligence for Robotics: Sensing, Learning, and Embodied Manipulation
slides.highlight: This review explores vision-based tactile sensors and learning methods for contact-rich tasks, providing a framework for enhancing embodied manipulation relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A comprehensive review of vision-based tactile sensors (VBTSs) integrating hardware design, AI learning, and simulation.
card.key_idea: Frames VBTSs as an integrated pipeline, categorizing hardware by elastomer, shape, and optics, while mapping learning methods from low-level signal processing to tactile foundation models.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the text is a survey review of existing literature rather than an experimental study with specific metrics.
card.limitation: Hardware design is task-specific, meaning no universal architecture exists; models often struggle to generalize across different sensor optical geometries.

slides.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL TACTILE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: HiTac-WAM introduces a hierarchical model that forecasts contact states, 3D deformation, and slip risk to improve planning and execution in contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: HiTac-WAM improves contact-rich manipulation by forecasting hierarchical tactile consequences to rank and verify action candidates.
card.key_idea: A world action model using a directed hierarchy (contact $\rightarrow$ deformation $\rightarrow$ slip risk) with stop-gradient conditioning and directed attention to predict tactile outcomes for candidate actions.
card.evaluation: Tested on chip grasping, blackboard erasing, and USB insertion. Real-robot success increased from 31.1% (baseline) to 72.2% (full system).
card.limitation: Forecast quality on model-generated chunks wasn't evaluated separately, and predicted slip risk is not calibrated for online detection.

slides.title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that spatially distributed tactile feedback reduces the gap between teleoperated and natural human trajectories, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating and aligning human proficiency through force-based views.

card.one_liner: Spatially distributed tactile feedback makes teleoperated robot movements more natural, consistent, and human-like.
card.key_idea: A 32-DoF cutaneous shape display reproduces localized deformations from a vision-based tactile sensor, supplementing bilateral kinesthetic force feedback.
card.evaluation: 12 participants performed button discrimination and peg-rolling tasks; results used DTW distance, completion time, and NASA-TLX, showing 29–79% reduced trajectory deviation.
card.limitation: Evaluated using only a 2-DoF system and two specific tasks, which may not generalize to higher-DoF dexterous manipulation.

slides.title: US-VLA: An Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Abdominal Scanning
slides.tldr: VISION-LANGUAGE-ACTION MODEL FOR AUTOMATED ULTRASOUND SCANNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a vision-language-action model for automated ultrasound probe manipulation, contributing to the development of embodied AI for clinical interactions relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: US-VLA is a vision-language-action model for automated, semantically-guided abdominal ultrasound probe manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines a pre-trained VLM with a US foundation model (USFM) and an ultrasound-aware expert fusion module to map clinical goals and real-time feedback to actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on US-VLA-Data (320 trajectories) across five abdominal tasks; achieved 84% average success rate, outperforming $\pi_0$ baselines in success and efficiency.

slides.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark to evaluate how policies physically interact with deformable objects. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of interaction states.

card.one_liner: A visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for evaluating both task success and physical interaction quality in deformable-object manipulation.
card.key_idea: Introduces SoftVTBench with 4,000 demonstrations and a Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR) using hidden FEM states to penalize excessive object compression.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Diffusion Policy, π0.5, and FastWAM across ID/OOD settings; results show TSR often masks physical failures (0.7-24% of successes violate deformation limits).
card.limitation: The deformation tolerance is an operational simulation criterion, not a real-world material-failure or damage threshold.

slides.title: ReForce: Learning Force-aware Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: ReForce enables robot actions to reproduce intended human contact forces, supporting the multimodal perception of physical interaction and engagement required for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: ReForce adapts kinematically retargeted human motions using online force feedback to improve dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop force tracker, trained on large-scale simulated hand-object interactions, predicts joint-command residuals to align robot fingertip forces with human-demonstrated contact targets.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation and real-world tasks (paper-cup grasping, tongs) against replay and admittance control; showed lower force-tracking error and better contact engagement.
card.limitation: Relies on normal fingertip forces only and lacks visual observations for task-aware reference generation.

slides.title: ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning
slides.highlight: This system utilizes vibrotactile feedback and multi-modal demonstration collection to improve success rates in contact-critical tasks, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills through ego-exo views and force-based feedback.

card.one_liner: ViHaTeleop is a low-cost, lightweight visual-haptic system improving success rates in contact-critical dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines SLAM-based wrist tracking, fisheye hand tracking, and LRA vibrotactile feedback with a tactile-aware retargeting constraint to ensure parallel fingertip alignment for better sensing.
card.evaluation: User study (9 participants) across 6 tasks showed success rate gains (+2.2% to +15.6%) and improved subjective confidence. Visual-tactile policies outperformed vision-only policies.
card.limitation: Small user sample size (n=9), lack of external ground-truth accuracy benchmarks, and limited training data for imitation learning.
